newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran says to repatriate Afghans via Turkmenistan.
newsitem.headline: Iran says to repatriate Afghans via Turkmenistan.

text.p: Iran plans to repatriate many of the more than 1.4 million Afghan refugees living in the country through neighbouring Turkmenistan, an Iranian official said on Tuesday.

Ahmad Hosseini, Iran's top official in charge of refugees, said the plan to return home the Afghan refugees was being carried out on a voluntary basis and in cooperation with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), Tehran radio said. .

Hosseini did not say how many of the 1.4 million Afghans living in Iran would be covered by the repatriation plan. In March he said some 200,000 would be repatriated under the plan and the United Nations had pledged $43 million for their settlement.

Areas of Afghanistan bordering Iran are controlled by the Taleban government and the plan apparently intends to return the refugees to regions under the control of deposed president Burhanuddin Rabbani whom Tehran recognises as the legitimate Afghan head of state.
A similar plan had to be abandoned last year because of the factional fighting in Afghanistan.
Tehran officials say the refugees are a burden on the economy. Official unemployment is 10.7 percent in a country of about 60 million Iranians.
Iran set a deadline in January for Iranian employers to fire illegal aliens, mostly Afghan workers, but residents said the drive appeared to have had little impact.

Millions of Afghans fled across the border after the Soviet invasion in 1979, creating one of the world's biggest refugee problems. The number of Afghans in Iran peaked at around three million in the mid-1980s.
Many returned home after the fall of the Soviet-installed government in Kabul in 1992, but the flow started again with the ensuing civil war.
Up to 1.5 million Afghans have been repatriated since 1993 but the country's civil war has slowed the return of the refugees to almost a complete halt.
Iran is home to two million refugees, who also include 600,000 from Iraq, making it the world's most important host country, according to the UNHCR.
